verses.text: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.
And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: "See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."
Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
But God found fault with the people and said: "Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.

For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more."
By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.

context.author: Unknown. The letter does not name its author. Paul, Barnabas, Apollos, and others have been suggested.
context.genre: A sermon in letter form, rich with Old Testament quotations
context.audience: Jewish Christians tempted to go back to old patterns under pressure
context.setting: The main point: we have a high priest seated at God’s right hand, serving in the true tent in heaven. Earthly priests serve in a copy and shadow. Jesus is mediator of a better covenant, as promised in Jeremiah 31, which the writer quotes in full.
context.custom: The tabernacle was modeled on a heavenly pattern (Exodus 25:40). The writer treats the earthly system as a pointer to a better reality. Calling the first covenant "obsolete and aging" (v.13) may suggest that the temple was still standing but its system was passing away.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 9 describes the earthly tabernacle and the better sacrifice.
context.timelineBible: Jeremiah 31:31-34 is the longest Old Testament quotation in the New Testament. Exodus 25:40 supports the heavenly pattern.
context.sparkNotes: We have such a high priest, seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven, minister in the true tent. Priests here serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. But Christ has obtained a ministry that is as much more excellent as the covenant he mediates is better. The Lord promises a new covenant: I will put my laws into their minds and write them on their hearts, and I will remember their sins no more. In speaking of a new covenant, he makes the first one obsolete.

translation.meaning: A go-between who brings two parties into agreement.
Can mean covenant or a will (testament). Both meanings are used in chapter 9.

otBackground.note: Make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.
A new heart and a new spirit.

overview.summary: Jesus serves in the true tent in heaven as mediator of the new covenant promised by Jeremiah, with laws on hearts and sins forgiven.

history.t: Hebrews says priests "offer gifts according to the law" (8:4), in the present tense. Some take this to mean that the temple still stood when the letter was written. Others think the writer is describing the system as Scripture sets it out and not what was happening at the time.
The new covenant was promised by Jeremiah in the early 6th century BC, around the time the temple fell to Babylon (Jeremiah 31:31-34).

customs.t: Shadows show a shape without substance.
Contrasts with writing on stone tablets.

archaeology.t: Full-scale models, such as the one at Timna Park in Israel, show the layout of the desert tent from the description in Exodus. No remains of the tabernacle itself have been found.

The Arch of Titus in Rome, built soon after AD 81, shows soldiers carrying the menorah and other spoils from the Jerusalem temple, destroyed in AD 70. The sacrifices Hebrews describes could no longer be offered after that.

overview.discussion: Jeremiah says God will write his law on hearts. How do I see God changing me from the inside, not just by rules?
overview.book: The letter to the Hebrews · 13 chapters. A polished sermon showing that Jesus fulfills and surpasses the old covenant.
overview.author: Unknown

Hebrews 8:13 says that what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear. After the temple fell in AD 70 the sacrifices it describes could no longer be offered.
